findings.title: Monitor reap is not sandbox-init cessation: abort closes a success barrier into EOF release
source_trace: NetworkAttachment.abort persists stop and registry.stop_runtest sends SIGKILL only to the retained bwrap monitor pidfd. The donor remains the sole monitor waiter.
When that monitor has been reaped, abort treats donor_proc.returncode != None as sufficient to close block_write. It does not establish sandbox-init or native whole-unit cessation.
The pinned bwrap sandbox-init is blocked at read(opt_block_fd,...,1). It ignores the return count and byte. EOF therefore proceeds to payload setup/fork/exec.

That sandbox-init has not yet established its own --die-with-parent: do_init installs PDEATHSIG after the block-fd read and payload fork. The monitor installs its separate parent-death signal in the monitor only, after raw_clone. Killing/reaping monitor can leave sandbox-init alive at the barrier.

A subsequent abort from the existing unit finally closes the retained writer and can release this orphaned child without slirp readiness, after cancellation. KillMode=control-group on later owner exit is eventual cleanup, not proof that this execution window never occurred. Owner death also closes the writer automatically.
findings.required_fix: Use a native success-only barrier, or prove the exact sandbox-init/whole child lineage has ceased before every failed writer closure, including owner-death cuts. Never equate monitor returncode with that proof.
findings.smallest_reusable_path: A narrow change in the selected bwrap block-fd consumer that requires an exact one-byte success token and otherwise fails before payload fork is the smallest local success-only semantic repair; retain existing FileOwner/registry/slirp architecture. It needs an independently reviewed matched bwrap rebuild and new exact binary/status/runtime pins. A stop-only alternative must prove child-lineage cessation first; simply retaining the writer until FileOwner exit remains insufficient.

findings.title: Network setup creates a separate startup clock and permits late helper spawn/barrier release
source_trace: NetworkAttachment assigns its own monotonic()+5 startup_end before DNS allocation. StatusCustody is constructed only afterwards and assigns a later independent monotonic()+5 anchor. Slow DNS preparation is outside the later status preparation window.

NetworkAttachment.current checks only original outer deadline/reserve, not startup_end. Constructor/provider checks, namespace acquisition and _start_helper can cross the startup limit; Popen is still attempted if the second-userns loop needs no iteration or its final identity call crosses the limit.

_ready checks startup_end before select but not after select/read/EOF. On final marker EOF it returns; attach_before_payload calls current (outer deadline only) and performs a further fallible owner.require_current before writing the barrier. A return after the startup deadline can therefore release payload.

The last helper-pidfd observation is the earlier select. There is no fresh helper/donor liveness check after the potentially slow current/owner verification before release. Later status rejection or finish detection cannot undo a payload already released.
findings.required_fix: Allocate one startup_end at the existing composition boundary before network/status preparation and pass that same unchanged value into both retained objects. Preserve the root status F1 owned-O_PATH contour acquisition and F2 startup fences. Fence network allocation/provider returns/namespace work/helper Popen/ready read and release before and after fallible operations, and require fresh retained helper/donor liveness immediately before the sole successful release. Finish/cleanup must continue using the original outer deadline and reserve, not a new five-second budget.

Namespace transition or helper preflight crosses startup_end: no Popen/release
Ready select/read EOF or owner verification returns after startup_end: no release

findings.title: The exact unit kills its own mandatory Unix-connect negative control
findings.reason: SystemCallFilter=~connect sendto sendmsg sendmmsg io_uring_setup io_uring_enter io_uring_register has no SystemCallErrorNumber or errno suffix. Installed 259.5 sources default to SECCOMP_ERROR_NUMBER_KILL. boundary_controls() intentionally calls AF_UNIX connect and only catches OSError. If the configured filter is enforced, that call terminates the payload with SIGSYS instead of producing the required negative observation; DNS NSS may trigger it earlier. No compiler phase can follow this mandatory path. The payload finally completion notification is also not reliable after this native termination.
findings.repair: Choose an explicit denial action compatible with the required controls, ordinarily SystemCallErrorNumber=EPERM while retaining the same denied syscall set. Bind its actual D-Bus signed-integer property in inactive and running typed validation (typed_value currently has no i support). Alternatively execute intentional death controls in a separately owned child and verify their actual outcome without killing the build owner. Do not remove the denial.

findings.title: Normal managed administrator route has no native-network execution admission gate
findings.trigger: Fresh normal-product/operator process with no ordinary UserScope engaged, valid installed pins and a public navigation URL; no native-browser CDP/egress capability exists.
source_trace: compose_product installs the managed browser configuration while NORMAL_TOOLSETS still includes hermes-cli, whose core tools include browser_*.
native_browser_check and check_browser_requirements return installed/registry readiness after checking only the local host and payload pins.

guard_tool returns for current()==None; browser_task_key explicitly chooses the operator namespace. _run_browser_command selects local_readiness, then _spawn_and_collect reaches Popen. There is no native loopback/page-egress admission check on this path.
The manifest acceptance text and execution-dependency.json are documentary; neither is consulted at dispatch/spawn. backend=off means built-in browser tools, not disabled browser execution.
findings.impact: The exact source does NOT fail closed on its declared unimplemented CDP/page-egress boundary for the normal operator route. Unchanged ordinary SAFE blocks ordinary registry calls only and cannot serve as the global execution barrier. This is an actual path beyond the claimed source-only boundary, not a restatement that public URL prechecks are insufficient.
findings.minimal_coherent_repair: Require a non-forgeable browser-specific capability from the existing execution/containment owner before any managed browser session, supervisor or command effect, including operator/administrator and normal installer/start routes. Until that capability is implemented and accepted, dispatch must deterministically refuse while source/install readiness remains separately reportable. Do not make local_runtime presence, administrator status, manifest text or a config boolean a network grant; retain existing ordinary SAFE pending explicit joined admission.
findings.required_control: Real normal registry dispatch with valid installation but missing/wrong/revoked browser execution admission must produce zero CLI, supervisor and network effects for both operator and ordinary identities. Later live proof must separately establish owned CDP/stream transport and OS-enforced page egress.

findings.title: Managed first navigation can connect an ambient CDP supervisor before rejecting BROWSER_CDP_URL
findings.trigger: BROWSER_CDP_URL is present when a first managed navigation reaches the registered handler, including after schema readiness was cached or through direct registry dispatch.
source_trace: browser_navigate calls _get_session_info before _run_browser_command and therefore before local_readiness/require_sandbox_host.
_get_session_info creates the managed local record but retains the unconditional _ensure_cdp_supervisor call for non-Lightpanda sessions.

The unchanged supervisor resolver prefers os.environ[BROWSER_CDP_URL], performs requests.get(.../json/version), and may start a WebSocket supervisor. Only the later local_readiness rejects the ambient BROWSER_* variable.
registry.dispatch calls the handler directly after scope guard; it does not rerun check_fn.
findings.impact: The promise that ambient CDP/config injection refuses before effects is false: arbitrary endpoint discovery and attachment can occur before the eventual refusal. The session record itself still says local with cdp_url=None, so this side effect is outside the retained managed session provenance.
findings.minimal_coherent_repair: For a managed local session, skip legacy override/supervisor resolution entirely unless a separately admitted owned endpoint is explicitly supplied by the eventual boundary. Perform managed policy, ambient environment and execution-admission validation before session/janitor/supervisor creation. Do not rely on registry discovery readiness as a dispatch guard.
findings.required_control: Inject BROWSER_CDP_URL into normal registry navigation and prove no resolver, requests, supervisor, session creation or CLI call occurs; test the real consumer chain instead of replacing _ensure_cdp_supervisor with a no-op.

findings.title: An unconfirmed revocation teardown bypasses termination of the in-flight CLI
findings.trigger: Admission is revoked after Popen but before the daemon publishes its PID, or while teardown identity/signal/cessation cannot be confirmed.
source_trace: The wait loop calls _check_session_authority. check_browser raises ScopeDenied, then _check_session_authority calls _force_reap_browser_session before returning the denial.
Managed _release_session_resources raises RuntimeError for missing PID/identity or surviving daemon. That RuntimeError replaces the PermissionError.

_spawn_and_collect only runs its active-client stop branch for PermissionError or TimeoutExpired. RuntimeError escapes to _dispatch_browser_command, which converts it into a normal error result; it never kills/waits for the already-created client.
findings.impact: A revoked operation can leave its native client alive and able to complete daemon/Chrome startup after the tool returned failure. Retaining STOP_UNCONFIRMED in the dictionary does not stop this in-flight capability.
findings.minimal_coherent_repair: Separate authority refusal from best-effort teardown outcome, and put client termination/collection plus native-custody reporting in an unconditional post-Popen exceptional-exit path. Preserve the original refusal and attach STOP_UNCONFIRMED without allowing a teardown exception to skip the active client stop. Do not re-admit or recreate the session.
findings.required_control: Revoke an in-flight client before PID publication and separately inject identity/signal failure. In each case observe original-client stop/wait attempted, output discarded, no replacement, retained unresolved custody, and eventual complete owned-scope cessation before acceptance.

findings.title: Managed teardown discards custody when only the daemon is known dead
findings.trigger: The daemon PID is dead/zombie while Chromium descendants or listeners survive; alternatively the native best-effort tree terminator kills the daemon but cannot enumerate or kill every descendant.
source_trace: Managed _release_session_resources tests _pid_exists only for the daemon. A pre-dead daemon bypasses _kill_verified_daemon entirely.
After termination it again checks only the daemon, then removes the active record and socket directory.

The reused _terminate_host_pid suppresses descendant enumeration/signalling failures and returns no complete-cessation result. The separate process-registry survivor/cgroup mechanisms are not used by this browser path.
findings.impact: Known-unproved whole-tree custody is converted into successful cleanup, enabling protocol retry/new session while an old browser or endpoint may survive. This is a source-level false closure, beyond merely having not yet collected live cessation evidence.
findings.minimal_coherent_repair: Keep managed custody and STOP_UNCONFIRMED until the existing stop owner proves the entire exact owned process/cgroup/listener scope empty. A missing/dead leader or successful signal must not release the record. Bind cleanup and retry to that authoritative result; retain durable evidence if a process exits or the host shuts down.
findings.required_control: Leader-dead/child-alive, child enumeration denied, rejected child signal, zombie leader and surviving owned listener must all retain custody and prohibit replacement. Acceptance requires independent full owned-cgroup cessation observation.

findings.title: Daemon identity verification and kill use different process generations
findings.source_basis: unchanged helper reused by the new managed cleanup branch; directly relevant inherited custody defect
findings.trigger: The verified daemon exits and its PID is reused between _verify_reapable_browser_daemon and _terminate_verified_daemon.
source_trace: _verify_reapable_browser_daemon checks name/argv/socket-dir binding and returns only a boolean.
_terminate_verified_daemon then obtains a NEW get_process_start_time value and gives that value to ProcessRegistry._terminate_host_pid.
The process registry compares against that newly captured value, so a replacement process can pass even though it was never the process whose browser/socket identity was verified.
findings.impact: The new managed cleanup path inherits a real PID-reuse window in which an unrelated process tree can be signalled. A fresh fingerprint obtained after identity verification does not establish retained ownership.
findings.minimal_coherent_repair: Carry one stable process identity from verification through termination (prefer the existing owner/cgroup or pidfd mechanism); verify the start identity before and after name/socket binding and require the same generation immediately before signalling. Never replace a missing retained identity with a freshly observed foreign generation. Treat mismatch/unknown as STOP_UNCONFIRMED.
findings.required_control: A controlled PID-generation change between binding verification and termination must issue zero signals to the replacement; ordinary unrelated-PID and denied identity probes must also retain custody.

findings.title: One revoked STOP_UNCONFIRMED session prevents janitor cleanup of all later sessions
findings.trigger: At least two sessions are present; the first revoked entry cannot be reaped, for example because launch was attempted but no daemon PID was published.
source_trace: The new revocation loop directly calls _force_reap_browser_session without a per-session exception boundary.
The first RuntimeError aborts the entire cleanup pass before later revoked entries and before inactivity cleanup.
The worker catches only around the whole pass, so the same first retained revoked entry aborts subsequent passes again.
findings.impact: One unresolved browser can indefinitely prevent revocation/idle teardown of unrelated principals in the shared process. Retaining the first session is correct; abandoning independent session cleanup is not.
findings.minimal_coherent_repair: Isolate each session teardown outcome within the revocation loop, retain and report its unresolved custody, and continue independent entries and normal inactivity processing. Preserve exact session identity and do not clear failure records merely to make the next pass green.
findings.required_control: Two actual retained principals: first revocation teardown refuses, second revocation teardown still runs in the same pass; repeat with an independently idle session and ensure no custody record is silently discarded.

findings.title: Managed path launches even when interruption is already pending
findings.trigger: is_interrupted() is already true before a managed command begins.
source_trace: The managed branch replaces _browser_command_preflight with local_readiness, bypassing the existing preflight interrupt check.
The new managed interrupt check is inside the polling loop, after Popen and after session/socket/config effects.
findings.impact: A cancelled turn can create a native client and possibly daemon/Chrome/network effects, then try to tear them down. This regresses the existing refuse-before-spawn interrupt behavior.
findings.minimal_coherent_repair: Check the same original interrupt state before managed session/effect admission and immediately before Popen; keep the in-flight polling check as well. Do not reset interrupt state or allocate a replacement task budget.
findings.required_control: An already-interrupted normal managed dispatch must produce zero client/supervisor/browser effects, alongside a separate in-flight interruption stop control.

findings.title: The managed command deadline is converted back into a fresh timeout inside dispatch
findings.trigger: Authority/configuration checks between the outer remaining-time calculation and _spawn_and_collect consume appreciable time, including the retry path.
source_trace: _run_browser_command computes one deadline, then remaining at line 1033.
run_fenced and _dispatch_browser_command perform more authority/config reads before _spawn_and_collect is entered.

_spawn_and_collect sets command_deadline = now + timeout, where timeout is that earlier remaining value. Time consumed between the two points is granted again instead of charged to the original deadline.
findings.impact: The source does not fully implement the claimed original command deadline. A delayed pre-spawn authority path can launch after the outer deadline; the existing test replaces _dispatch_browser_command and therefore cannot observe this.
findings.minimal_coherent_repair: Pass the absolute monotonic deadline through fencing, dispatch, preparation and collection; derive remaining time only at the operation that consumes it. Keep one original budget across protocol and donor launch retries, and bind final execution to the existing task/cgroup deadline rather than refreshing per-command capability.
findings.required_control: Advance the observed monotonic clock during real dispatch/fence preparation beyond the original deadline; verify no Popen occurs and no retry replenishes it. This must exercise _spawn_and_collect rather than replacing dispatch.

findings.title: Relative builtin/Path opens bypass the file fence
findings.detail: The audit hook resolves every string path but applies write and credential restrictions only when the original path is absolute. The os.open replacement covers only calls through os.open; builtin open and Path.open/read_text/write_text use their own IO implementation. A relative builtin open('../outside-file','w') therefore falls through the audit hook without requiring the resolved path to remain under R. The same branch permits relative reads of the protected credential basenames outside R. This is a static counterexample; it was not executed and no actual outside write/read is claimed.

findings.title: OfflineBoundaryStop does not stop the pytest contour
findings.detail: OfflineBoundaryStop inherits directly from BaseException, but pytest catches BaseException during setup/call/teardown. The inspected _pytest/runner.py:249-267 and 360-366 re-raises only Exit and, normally, KeyboardInterrupt. Controls.py logs failures and does not set session.shouldstop or re-raise the boundary exception; its pytest argv has no stop-on-first-failure option. A denied effect in a fixture/test can therefore become one failed report while subsequent work continues. The offending syscall is still refused, but whole-contour cessation is not guaranteed.
findings.implication: The declared 'BaseException stopping entire contour' claim is false for the inspected pytest route; later reports require an actual execution reconciliation.
findings.bounded_remediation: Provide an explicit, non-swallowable contour stop with truthful exit/cleanup evidence. Do not re-run the stopped multiprocessing case.

findings.title: The one-shot wall alarm can be swallowed without a remaining wall limit
findings.detail: SIGALRM raises ordinary TimeoutError. A product handler or pytest's BaseException capture can consume it. signal.alarm is one-shot and the guard does not recheck the monotonic deadline after it fires. RLIMIT_CPU=600 remains a CPU-time bound, not a wall-time bound, so sleeping/blocked later tests can exceed both the intended per-process wall duration and original assignment deadline.
findings.implication: This snapshot cannot establish a hard finite wall deadline. No actual overrun is asserted. Ancillary native-guard-hardening.json already disclaims a general hard-wall guarantee for the original project guard; its different native_guard.py is outside this snapshot.

findings.title: The scoped launcher tests supply socket stdio where the launcher requires FIFO or null.
findings.evidence: run() defaults to Node spawnSync stdio=[ignore,pipe,pipe]. Authoritative Node/Unix libuv source implements those pipe streams through UV_CREATE_PIPE and SOCK_STREAM socketpair. C accepts only S_ISFIFO, or a null character-device number, at FD0-2. Therefore even on an ABI6-capable kernel the first positive SELF_OK fixture is predicted to exit125 before exec; the later IPC and inherited-FD checks do not qualify their intended boundary.
findings.impact: The new real primitive qualification entry is not runnable with its claimed positive behavior on the cited Unix Node/libuv implementation. findings.bounded_fix: Launch the owned primitive fixtures with actual caller-compatible OS pipes/null using the existing bounded qualification mechanism, retain a sole drainer and original budget, and verify descriptor types/ownership. Keep socket stdio as an explicit negative. Do not accept arbitrary S_ISSOCK merely to make the test green. Preserve same-domain UNIX/network positives and outside-domain sensitivity controls.

findings.title: Checkpoint failure prevents the requested stop
findings.finding: stop_runtest latches stop_requested in memory, then calls _runtest_checkpoint before it reaches _terminate_host_pid. A failed checkpoint write/readback (including a missing or malformed file) raises out of the stop method, so a live, identity-known process receives no termination request. kill_process forwards this method directly, and kill_all also aborts its list comprehension on that exception. The source hard-deadline/outer boundary remains only a prerequisite, not an implemented substitute.
static_failure_trace: Known live runtest session; owner requests cancellation.
Checkpoint cannot persist the changed stop flag, or its readback fails.
_runtest_checkpoint raises; identity-aware termination below it is skipped.
findings.smallest_connected_fix: Keep admission/spawn fenced on persistence failure, but make an actual cancellation attempt through the existing reviewed identity-safe stop path independent of successful diagnostic persistence. Preserve STOP_UNCONFIRMED and the retained handle when persistence or cessation is unknown; do not report completion or retry launch.
required_controls: Inject write failure, missing checkpoint, malformed JSON and readback mismatch while a real isolated owned child is alive; verify stop is attempted, donor remains sole drainer and custody is retained until observed closure.
Verify one failing stop does not prevent attempted cleanup of other already-owned targets.

findings.title: Post-Popen exceptions occur outside donor cleanup and draining
findings.finding: The donor enters its try/finally only after custody.spawn returns. That callback performs the real Popen, PID/SID discovery, strict checkpoint readback and several durable backend/custody writes before returning. Any exception after Popen therefore escapes before donor communicate/stop/settle is established. session.process retains a handle, but no donor drainer/reaper runs; the actual outer caller that could cover this case is not implemented in this snapshot. This is an exception-safety hole in addition to the explicitly acknowledged process-crash interval.
static_failure_trace: Popen succeeds and the child starts.
Registry post-spawn checkpoint or owner backend-start/runtest-custody write fails.
custody.spawn raises before donor proc assignment completes; donor try/finally is never entered.
findings.smallest_connected_fix: Bring every operation after a successful Popen under the same existing owner lifecycle, with one accessible actual handle and exactly one donor drain/reap path even when provenance persistence fails. Route failure to existing identity-safe stop plus retained custody; do not add a second drainer, detached manager or replay.
required_controls: Fault after actual Popen but before PID persistence, after PID persistence, while reading stat, and at each backend receipt write.
Prove no duplicate communicate/reader, no unowned child, exact retained reservation and no second Popen on retry.
Retain output and provenance sufficient to diagnose partial/startup failures.

findings.title: Readback does not make the shared checkpoint ordered and crash durable
findings.finding: The new reservation relies on _write_checkpoint plus readback as durable custody. The mixin snapshots _running under the registry lock but releases that lock before atomic_json_write; another older snapshot can overwrite a later acknowledged reservation/PID record. atomic_json_write is also called with its default fsync_dir=False, so successful readback does not prove that the replacement directory entry survives power loss. Recovery cannot retain an intent that was overwritten or not durably named.
static_failure_trace: Writer A snapshots the shared registry before the new reservation and stalls before replace.
Writer B adds/reserves the runtest, writes its record, reads it back and proceeds.
Writer A replaces the file with its stale snapshot, removing the acknowledged reservation.
Separately, a power loss after replace but before directory durability can lose the just-acknowledged checkpoint entry.
findings.smallest_connected_fix: Serialize checkpoint snapshot-through-replacement across every writer of this same existing registry checkpoint, and make critical runtest persistence confirm file and parent-directory durability with failures propagated to admission. Keep stop exception safety from F1; no parallel checkpoint registry or broad new manager.
required_controls: Controlled interleaving of an older generic checkpoint write with reservation, PID attachment and stop-latch writes; the newest custody record must remain recoverable.
Critical file/directory fsync failure and restart from the last durable record; retain unresolved intent and never replay.

findings.title: Contradictory exit-5 and post-session collection evidence is admissible
findings.finding: census checks failed phases only when terminal_exit==0. A complete failed setup/call/teardown sequence followed by session_finish(exit=5), with backend exit5, returns RUNTEST_REPORTED even though it contains a failed phase. Also collection does not require not session_finished: session_finish(exit=5) followed by a collection event deselecting every expected item is accepted as complete RUNTEST_REPORTED. observe treats that status as next_phase_admissible. Neither trace is a truthful canonical no-tests result. failure_observed is retained in the first trace, but its contradictory top-level evidence is still treated as admissible; no product-acceptance flag is set.
findings.smallest_connected_fix: Make session completion terminal for all event kinds and reconcile exit5 with actual zero-selected/no-runtest semantics before returning an admissible status. Reject contradictory receipts while retaining any observed product failures and partial evidence.
required_controls: Complete failed-call trace with terminal/session exit5 must not be RUNTEST_REPORTED or next-phase-admissible.
session_finish then collection, with sequences renumbered and all expected items deselected, must be rejected.
Positive genuine all-deselected exit5, setup-skip, xfail, non-strict xpass, strict-xpass failure and partial hard-exit controls.

actual_failure.meaning: v259.5 object verification rejects the data hash table bucket head offset via VALID64 and returns EBADMSG. The 16656 position is the containing object position reported by the verifier, not proof that damage begins or is confined to byte 16656.

actual_failure.query_correlation: Same exact archive path appears in retained query iteration errors. Query rc0 and graceful skipping cannot clear the separate integrity failure. Other retained error offsets were not audited; restoring this file alone is not a claim that every diagnostic will disappear.

basis.claim: Installed journalctl manual is systemd 259.5 and defines --verify as consistency checking, with authenticity checking conditional on FSS/key. The verify action reports PASS/FAIL; it does not restore corrupt data.

Reviewed CLI option/action surfaces provide verification, rotation and vacuuming, but no repair/recover command. This conclusion is scoped to the reviewed supported interface; it is not a theorem against all possible offline forensic reconstruction.
The format recovery rule preserves a corrupt old file and writes a new one; readers may skip corrupt regions. This is continuity/salvage behavior, not restoration of complete original history.

.journal~ denotes corrupted or uncleanly closed material, and archived files are no longer written. journal_file_dispose performs a rename without inspecting or modifying file contents; the suffix does not identify a second clean backup.
The reader explicitly accepts .journal~. Existing exact saved verify proves this file is structurally corrupt; renaming back or rotating the current writer cannot repair its contents.

findings.title: Transport read classification permits undeclared mutating commands, including after Driver closure
findings.evidence: ParentTransport.classify checks whether the literal show/list-jobs occurs anywhere in argv and excludes only a short list of exact tokens. It accepts systemctl --user kill show, systemctl --user mask show, and systemctl --user try-restart show (show is the operand, not the verb). journalctl --vacuum-time=1s bypasses the bare --vacuum-time exclusion. Function-only guarded Popen controls dispatched these as kind=read with uncertain=False; try-restart was accepted in phase=cleanup after close_driver. No actual command was executed.
findings.why_blocks: The new parent boundary claims exact read clients and no future mutators after Driver closure, but does not enforce that scope. Driver.manager(effect=True) does not communicate an expected effect class to ParentTransport; Driver.__init__ also reopens recipe.json rather than consuming the already verified source buffer. An altered/reopened recipe entry can therefore be classified as a read instead of matching one of the approved start argv. This is a concrete guard defect; it is not evidence that the immutable reviewed recipe currently contains those commands or that arbitrary malicious same-UID code is contained.
findings.required_fix: Allow only the complete approved preflight, unit, job, manager and reload argv; validate the finite journal query grammar including option values, exact selected unit/manager/boot and allowed fields. Require a caller-expected effect class or equivalent invariant so start requests cannot fall through to the read lane. Preserve the verified recipe buffer or validate its exact read bytes before using it. Add negative controls for alternate mutating verbs and option=value syntax in admission, Driver and cleanup phases without widening privileges or introducing a broker.
